# How to clone your own voice with ElevenLabs, safely and with consent

> **In short:** In ElevenLabs, open **Voices**, click the plus icon, and choose **Instant Voice Clone**. Upload or record about 1–2 minutes of clear speech, name the voice, confirm you have the right and consent to clone it, and click **Save voice**. Clone only your own voice, and agree on a family code word in case someone tries a voice-clone scam call.

A voice clone is a digital copy of a voice that can read out any text you type. It's handy if you want to narrate your own videos or slideshows without recording every line. This guide follows ElevenLabs' official documentation for Instant Voice Cloning, and it's written for one use only: cloning **your own** voice.

## Before you start
-   **An ElevenLabs account.** Sign up at [elevenlabs.io](https://elevenlabs.io). Which plans include voice cloning is shown on the official ElevenLabs site.
-   **Your own voice, and only yours.** Never clone a friend's, a family member's, or a celebrity's voice, even as a joke.
-   **A quiet room and a microphone.** A phone or computer microphone works if the room is quiet.
-   **About 15 minutes,** including the recording.

## Step 1 — Record a clean sample
ElevenLabs' docs say about **1–2 minutes** of clear audio is enough: at least 1 minute, and more than 3 minutes adds little. The clone copies everything it hears, including breathing, background noise, echo, and music, so the recording matters more than its length.

-   Only one person speaks: you.
-   No background noise, echo, or music.
-   Keep the same tone and pace the whole time.
-   If you save the file as MP3, the docs recommend 192 kbps or higher.

💬 Example: Read two or three paragraphs from a book or article you like, out loud, in your normal speaking voice.

You'll know it worked when you play the file back and hear only your voice, clearly, with no other sounds.

## Step 2 — Start an Instant Voice Clone
Sign in to ElevenLabs and open the **Voices** section. Click the **plus icon**, then choose **Instant Voice Clone**.

**If it looks different:** Menus can change between versions. The ElevenLabs docs for Instant Voice Cloning describe the current steps.

You'll know it worked when you see the screen that asks for your audio.

## Step 3 — Add your audio and name the voice
Follow the on-screen steps to **upload** the file from Step 1, or **record** your sample right there. Then give the clone a name you'll recognize, such as "My narration voice."

You'll know it worked when your audio file and the name both show on the screen.

## Step 4 — Confirm consent and save
ElevenLabs asks you to confirm that you have the right and the consent to clone this voice. Since it's your own voice, you can confirm honestly. Then click **Save voice**.

You'll know it worked when the new voice appears under **Voices** → **My Voices**.

## Step 5 — Test it with new text
Under **My Voices**, find your clone and click **Use voice**. Type a sentence that was **not** in your recording and listen to the result.

💬 Example: "Welcome to my channel. Today I'm showing you three easy ways to organize a small kitchen."

You'll know it worked when the voice reads your new sentence and sounds like you.

## Use your clone safely
-   **Only your own voice.** Don't use a clone to pretend to be anyone, and don't make it say things you wouldn't say yourself.
-   **Tell people when it's AI.** If you post a video with your cloned voice, say that the voice was made with AI. Many platforms ask you to label realistic AI audio.
-   **Prepare your family for scam calls.** Criminals can copy a voice from short clips posted online and call relatives asking for money. Agree on a family code word, and if a "family member" calls in a panic, hang up and call them back on the number you know.
-   **Keep your original recordings.** You may want them again later.

## Common mistakes
-   **Recording in a noisy or echoing room:** The clone copies the noise too.
    *   **The fix:** Re-record in a quiet room with soft furnishings, close to the microphone.
-   **Changing your tone halfway through:** A mix of whispering and shouting confuses the clone.
    *   **The fix:** Read in one steady, natural voice from start to finish.
-   **Uploading a very long file:** More than about 3 minutes adds little, according to the docs.
    *   **The fix:** Pick your best 1–2 minutes.
-   **Testing with the same words you recorded:** That doesn't show how the clone handles new text.
    *   **The fix:** Always test with a fresh sentence.

## What this means for you
-   **In everyday life:** Narrate family slideshows or travel videos in your own voice without recording every line.
-   **For your business or work:** Read out short product updates or training clips in a consistent voice, and tell your audience that the voice is AI-made.
-   **If you're just getting started:** Begin with one short test sentence. If it doesn't sound right, improve the recording before anything else.

## Try it now
Record 1–2 minutes of yourself reading a favorite article in a quiet room, create an Instant Voice Clone in ElevenLabs, and test it with this sentence: *"Hi, this is my AI voice. I made it myself, and I'll always say when I use it."*
